es: Analizar un discurso breve, escrito y en audio: localizar la tesis, las técnicas (concesión, pregunta retórica, señalizadores), la apelación emocional y la llamada a la acción.

teaching.en: In the opening, the speaker states the thesis clearly, because a listener who hears a strong claim early can follow the rest of the argument.
teaching.es: En la apertura, el orador expone la tesis con claridad, porque un oyente que escucha pronto una afirmación sólida puede seguir el resto del argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis suele estar al principio; claim = afirmación que se defiende.
segments: In the opening, the speaker states the thesis clearly, because a listener who
hears a strong claim early can follow the rest of the argument.
teaching.audioText: In the opening, the speaker states the thesis clearly, because a listener who hears a strong claim early can follow the rest of the argument.

teaching.en: A speaker who can concede a point, for example by admitting that the plan is expensive, gains credibility with a sceptical audience.
teaching.es: Un orador que sabe admitir un punto, por ejemplo reconociendo que el plan es caro, gana credibilidad ante un público escéptico.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede a point: reconocer que el adversario tiene razón en algo; aumenta la credibilidad.
segments: A speaker who can concede a point, for example by admitting
that the plan is expensive, gains credibility with a sceptical audience.
teaching.audioText: A speaker who can concede a point, for example by admitting that the plan is expensive, gains credibility with a sceptical audience.

teaching.en: Phrases such as first, secondly and finally act as a signpost, helping listeners to see where the argument is going.
teaching.es: Expresiones como «primero», «en segundo lugar» y «por último» funcionan como señalizadores y ayudan al público a ver hacia dónde va el argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: Un signpost no añade información: guía al oyente por la estructura.
segments: Phrases such as first, secondly and finally act as a
signpost, helping listeners to see where the argument is going.
teaching.audioText: Phrases such as first, secondly and finally act as a signpost, helping listeners to see where the argument is going.

teaching.en: A rhetorical question is often used to appeal to the audience's feelings, which classical writers called pathos, rather than to logic.
teaching.es: Una pregunta retórica suele usarse para apelar a los sentimientos del público, lo que los autores clásicos llamaban pathos, más que a la lógica.
teaching.explanationEs: Appeal to + nombre: apelar a; pathos = apelación a la emoción.
segments: A rhetorical question is often used to appeal to the audience's
feelings, which classical writers called pathos, rather than to logic.
teaching.audioText: A rhetorical question is often used to appeal to the audience's feelings, which classical writers called pathos, rather than to logic.

teaching.en: The closing usually ends with a call to action, such as sign the petition tonight, and this is how a speaker tries to rally support.
teaching.es: El cierre suele terminar con una llamada a la acción, como «firma la petición esta noche», y así intenta el orador reunir apoyos.
teaching.explanationEs: La llamada a la acción pide algo concreto: quién, qué y cuándo.
segments: The closing usually ends with a call to action, such as sign the
petition tonight, and this is how a speaker tries to rally support.
teaching.audioText: The closing usually ends with a call to action, such as sign the petition tonight, and this is how a speaker tries to rally support.

teaching.en: To summarise, the speaker argues that the school needs a garden, uses a tricolon to build the claim and asks the audience to sign the petition.
teaching.es: En resumen, la oradora sostiene que el colegio necesita un huerto, usa un tricolon para construir la afirmación y pide al público que firme la petición.
teaching.explanationEs: Resumen: argues that + tesis; asks the audience to + acción.
segments: To summarise, the speaker argues that the school needs a garden, uses a
tricolon to build the claim and asks the audience to sign the petition.
teaching.audioText: To summarise, the speaker argues that the school needs a garden, uses a tricolon to build the claim and asks the audience to sign the petition.

prompt.es: Identifica la tesis en la apertura del discurso.

choices.text: The school should buy more bikes for students.
Students should stop riding bikes to school.
We must build a bike shelter this year.

feedback.es: La oradora presenta su afirmación principal con I believe: hay que construir un cobertizo para bicis este año.

hint.es: La tesis es lo que la oradora cree que hay que hacer.

origin.text: Our school has forty bikes but no safe place to park them. Every week, three are stolen. I believe we must build a bike shelter this year, and I will explain why.

prompt.es: Completa: «La oradora pide al público que firme la petición en la puerta.»

feedback.es: Con la oradora (tercera persona) el verbo es asks + persona + to + verbo.

hint.es: Verbo en tercera persona del singular: pide.

origin.text: At the end of the speech, the speaker ___ the audience to sign the petition at the door. This is her call to action.

prompt.es: Elige la técnica que domina el fragmento.

choices.text: Rhetorical questions built on contrast.
A thesis followed directly by a petition.
A concession that wins the audience over.

feedback.es: Las tres preguntas no esperan respuesta y oponen autos y personas, ruido y conversación.

origin.text: Do we want a city of cars, or a city of people? Do we want noise, or conversation? Do we want to hurry past each other, or to stop and talk?

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué quiere conseguir la oradora.

choices.text: A cheaper bus pass for students who live far away.
A safe route for students who walk to school.
A pavement for the teachers who walk to work.

feedback.es: El problema es una carretera sin acera y la tesis final pide un camino seguro para quienes van andando.

origin.audio: Good morning, everyone. Every day, three hundred students walk along a road without a pavement. Some of you may say that a path is expensive, and I accept that it is. First, though, think of the risk. Secondly, think of the cost of doing nothing. Finally, ask yourself this: would you let your own child cross that road? Today I will argue that our school needs a safe path, and I ask you to support it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con su función en el discurso.

pairs: I believe the school needs a garden.
Who wants lunch from a plastic box?
First, let us look at the cost.

feedback.es: Lo que se defiende es la tesis, la pregunta sin respuesta es retórica, la petición de actuar es la llamada y first guía al oyente.

pairs: I believe the school needs a garden.
Who wants lunch from a plastic box?
First, let us look at the cost.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La oradora termina pidiendo al público que firme.»

answer.text: The speaker ends by asking the audience to sign

feedback.es: Ends by asking + persona + to + verbo: así se resume la llamada a la acción.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige su tesis.

choices.text: Classes should finish earlier so students can study.
The council should build a second library.
The library should stay open later for students.

feedback.es: La oradora pide ampliar el horario de la biblioteca hasta las ocho; la pregunta y la petición de firmas apoyan esa tesis.

origin.audio: Good morning. Our library closes at four, yet most students finish class at half past four. Who can study in a closed library? Not me, not you, not anyone. Some will say that the council cannot afford longer hours, and I understand that worry. But think of what we lose: quiet rooms, free books and a place to work. Students need a library that opens late, so I am asking the council to keep it open until eight. Please add your name to the list at the door.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué menciona la preocupación del municipio.

choices.text: To win trust by admitting a fair objection.
To blame the council for wasting money.
To show that she expects the council to refuse.

feedback.es: Al decir I understand that worry, concede un punto al adversario antes de rebatirlo: así gana credibilidad.

origin.audio: Good morning. Our library closes at four, yet most students finish class at half past four. Who can study in a closed library? Not me, not you, not anyone. Some will say that the council cannot afford longer hours, and I understand that worry. But think of what we lose: quiet rooms, free books and a place to work. Students need a library that opens late, so I am asking the council to keep it open until eight. Please add your name to the list at the door.

prompt.es: Completa: «Usa una pregunta retórica para apelar a los sentimientos del público.»

feedback.es: Appeal to + nombre significa apelar a: la pregunta retórica busca mover los sentimientos.

origin.text: She opens by stating her thesis, then uses a rhetorical question to ___ to the audience's feelings before closing with a petition.

prompt.es: Resume el discurso: tesis y llamada a la acción.

answer.text: The speaker argues that the town needs an electric minibus and asks the audience to vote for it on Friday.
accepted: The speaker argues that the town needs an electric minibus and asks the audience to vote for it on Friday.
The speaker says that the town needs an electric minibus and invites the audience to vote on Friday.
The speaker claims that we need an electric minibus and asks people to vote for it on Friday.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen contiene la tesis (argues that…) y la llamada a la acción (asks the audience to…).

origin.text: The bus is late, the road is full and the air is dirty. Why should we accept this? Our town needs an electric minibus, and I ask you all to vote for it on Friday.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto busca la pregunta final de la oradora.

choices.text: To collect suggestions from the audience about plastic.
To make the audience see the problem in their own habits.
To introduce the figures that she will present next.

feedback.es: La pregunta final no busca una respuesta: tras tres ejemplos de reutilización, deja que el público vea por sí mismo la incoherencia de tirar el plástico.

origin.audio: We reuse paper. We reuse glass. We reuse cans. So why do we still throw away plastic? Nobody in this room can give me a good reason, and I suspect that nobody wants to.

prompt.es: Completa: «La apertura presenta la tesis del discurso.»

feedback.es: La tesis es la afirmación principal y se expone en la apertura.

origin.text: A good listener notes the claim made at the start. The opening states the ___ of the speech, and everything that follows supports it.

prompt.es: Elige la llamada a la acción del fragmento.

choices.text: The council must keep its promises about the river.
Our river is getting dirtier every year.
Join the clean-up on Sunday at nine.

feedback.es: La llamada a la acción es lo que se pide al público: unirse a la limpieza el domingo a las nueve.

origin.text: Our river is getting dirtier every year, and the council has promised action three times. Please join the clean-up on Sunday at nine, and bring gloves. Every pair of hands will help.
